motivation: In the frozen parent and first checkpoints the review movement strongly prefers the previously appetitive candidate polarity. Its side often reverses when both displayed polarities reverse, without a comparable change in recall. Test whether the use of one response for collection and review is an obstacle.

arms.reserved: Use existing hidden nodes 18/19 instead of 10/11 solely to emit the study-route movement. Same 20-node graph, same count of inherited and lifetime parameters, different motor coordinate at baseline.
arms.review: Add a zero-initialized scalar bias and 20 weights on the body's own current hidden activation to the usual motor logit only when choosing the review route.
arms.shared: Identically initialized 21 coefficients are active during all collection, review and terminal movements. Match parameter count, initial graph, optimization and total interactions to review.

comparison: All three arms start from the same uniform parent as the native core. The reserved port's baseline is explicitly different. Both learned-residual arms have identical initial actions and scores as the core. Reuse the core's exact training worlds and actual future motor payoff, retention schedule, start/stop, learning rate, gradient clip, and six+six birth cohorts. Local weights, biases and directed edges remain writable in all lives. Two fixed 8000-step endpoints per architecture/cohort, report the endpoint at 8000 and its 4000-step milestone. Tiny extra motor weights are inherited and not edited inside a life.
frozen_readout: On wholly new worlds, from each model's own trajectory compare its selected option against actually taking each side at random, forced opposite, and its own action redistributed across different private value histories while preserving the same public candidate and geometry. Remove the extra review projection at the menu without changing the inherited body, and freeze that single review write. Report actual terminal mean and all-four jointly, purchase-side polarity bias, ordinary two/four-item no-review retention, and whether these results transfer to new private maps.
